newsitem.title: UK: UK economy doing well, could do better - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK economy doing well, could do better - CBI.

text.p: Britain's economy is in good shape but should be able to close the prosperity gap between its major competitors further, Confederation of British Industry director-general Adair Turner said on Thursday.
He added that short-term prospects for inflation were good but warned against complacency.

Speaking at the CBI Scotland's annual dinner in Glasgow, Turner said productivity improvements in manufacturing, services and the privatised utilities, low and stable inflation and success in luring inward investments were all major achievements.

"But the big picture remains that while relative decline has been halted, we have not yet caught up with richer competitors," Turner said. "To do better, what we need is continuity, fiscal responsibility and improved investment."
He pleaded for fiscal responsibility in the run-up to elections which must be held by May 1997 and said one blot on the UK economy's copybook was the state of public finances.
"Borrowing has to be kept on a steady downward path - not allowed to let slip and then corrected with a jolt later."
Turner also said the government must address investment in education and transport infrastructure.
"In transport infrastructure...we under-invest significantly in comparison with competitor countries."
